summary: This House resolution supports designating March 2026 as Endometriosis Awareness Month, recognizes needs for earlier diagnosis and more research funding, and urges public education activities about the disease.

scores.thoughts: The resolution explicitly states commitment to 'supporting and funding endometriosis research' in paragraph (3). This directly endorses government expenditure on medical research, which aligns with expanding rather than reducing spending. The effect is limited because it is a non-binding resolution rather than an appropriations bill.
The bill contains no references to taxes, tax policy, revenue measures, or any fiscal mechanisms that would alter tax rates or structures.

The resolution addresses a gynecological disease by calling for early detection, treatment, provider education, culturally competent care, and research into therapies. These provisions engage the public-health and research dimensions of healthcare policy rather than promoting market-based or privatized approaches.
No provisions or language relate to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The text does not mention immigration, border policy, visas, or related enforcement matters.
Although endometriosis affects fertility and reproductive health, the resolution makes no reference to abortion access, restrictions, or reproductive rights.
No language addresses military budgets, defense programs, or national security spending.
The bill contains no environmental, climate, or regulatory provisions.
No provisions concern welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The resolution calls for awareness activities and provider education but does not address K-12 schooling, federal education funding, school choice, or privatization.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement appear in the text.
The resolution does not engage sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal-justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
While the bill endorses research funding, it does not discuss deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal restraint; any connection is too attenuated to register.
The text contains no provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
No language addresses foreign assistance, international aid, or related appropriations.
The resolution does not mention voting access, election integrity, voter ID, or electoral procedures.
No provisions relate to technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
Although the preamble notes employment impacts, the operative clauses do not address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
The bill does not engage religious exemptions, civil-rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
